title: Presumptive
subtitle: Lot Trace, Holds & Recall Notification

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday, October 12, 2027, Pacific Time, mid harvest in the Salinas Valley. At 05:50 Coastal Analytical Labs emails a presumptive positive for E. coli O157:H7 on a retained sample of lot PF1-27278-L2-B (Plant 1, line 2, shift B, produced October 5); the confirmation test will take 24 to 48 hours. The exercise starts at 06:00 as Recall Coordinator and VP Food Safety and Quality Dr. Imani Brooks opens the Recall Team call on the bridge (831) 555-0131. The signal time is 05:50 and the plan's measures run from it. Scope: every lot made on line 2 within 24 hours of the positive and the raw material lot FLD-SLG-R14-C-27277 from Santa Lucia Growers Ranch 14, Block C: five lots, PF1-27277-L2-B, PF1-27278-L2-A, PF1-27278-L2-B, PF1-27279-L2-A and PF1-27279-L2-B, 38,600 cases in all, shipped as 18,900 to the Stockton DC, 9,700 to the Phoenix DC, 7,400 to the Dallas DC and 2,600 direct to the co-packer Rivermark Kits in Fresno; use-by dates run to October 19 and about 40 percent has already sold through. Pressure points: MES holds within 30 minutes and physical holds at the DCs within 4 hours; Plant Manager Dwayne Pruitt stops line 2 for sanitation and swab series; the Traceability and Systems Lead Kevin Oyelaran's trace must reach the ship-to level for customers Harvest Table Markets (212 stores, category manager Joyce Whitlock), Cornerstone Grocers (140 Texas stores, buyer Eddie Navarro), Westline Foodservice (31 delivery points including hospitals and school districts) and Rivermark, whose receiving records are on paper (the last mock recall left 4 percent unmatched) and whose Caesar kits went on to national retail accounts; a Sonoran Cold Freight trailer with 1,320 cases is 14 hours out on the road to Dallas near Tucson and Dallas has already shipped 2,100 cases to 38 Cornerstone stores since 04:00; MES counts 38,600 cases but a WMS export says 38,540 and a draft press release says 'about 40,000'; at 09:30 the California Department of Public Health calls about three reported illnesses with a pending genetic match and asks for the distribution list; the FDA records request starts a 24-hour clock for a sortable spreadsheet; a food safety blogger posts at 11:00 that 'romaine is about to be recalled'; the President, Nathan Kowalczyk, must decide on the recall (class, depth, public warning) before confirmation results arrive, which the plan permits; the recall letter must carry the lot codes, quantity per customer, action, reply form and contacts and be sent to every direct customer within 4 hours of the decision; Cornerstone threatens to drop Pinecrest and demands replacement romaine while the VP Supply Chain Marcus Tillman can replace only about 60 percent of romaine volume in 48 hours (allocation rule, alternate source from spot growers); General Counsel Renata Voss notifies Trellis Mutual; the Communications Manager Tom Haskell's press release goes out with the retailers' agreement, and a Central Coast Courier reporter calls. Decisions the toolkit forms cover: hold or quarantine a lot, submit the trace result, declare the recall, notify customers, allocate supply, switch source, reroute a trailer and escalate to the executive. The SimCell plays the lab, FDA, CDPH, Arizona, Nevada and Texas agencies, the customers' category managers, the carriers, the grower, Rivermark, reporters, the blogger and consumers.
audience: VP Food Safety and Quality (Recall Coordinator)
constraints: Every Pinecrest email address uses the exercise domain pinecrestfresh.example; customers, growers, carriers, the co-packer, insurer and outlets use fictional .example domains; never a real brand, grower, retailer or outlet.

Lot codes follow the plant format PF<plant>-<yy><ddd>-L<line>-<shift> exactly, recall letters carry the elements in the recall notification procedure, and every count in a letter, release or FDA submission comes from the reconciliation table; documents are marked as exercise products; times are Pacific Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the President, General Counsel, plant and DC managers, FDA, CDPH and other agencies, the lab, customers, carriers, the grower, the co-packer, reporters and consumers are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Deciding before the facts are confirmed, getting one set of numbers across MES, WMS and paper records, and keeping the required notification order while regulators, customers and the media push to go first.
overview.threat: At 05:50 Pacific Time on Tuesday, October 12, 2027, during the Salinas Valley harvest, Coastal Analytical Labs emailed a presumptive positive for E. coli O157:H7 on a retained sample of lot PF1-27278-L2-B (Plant 1, line 2, shift B, produced October 5). Confirmation will take 24 to 48 hours. The scope covers every lot made on line 2 within 24 hours of the positive, plus raw material lot FLD-SLG-R14-C-27277 from Santa Lucia Growers Ranch 14, Block C. That makes five lots (PF1-27277-L2-B, PF1-27278-L2-A, PF1-27278-L2-B, PF1-27279-L2-A and PF1-27279-L2-B) totaling 38,600 cases. They shipped as 18,900 to the Stockton DC, 9,700 to the Phoenix DC, 7,400 to the Dallas DC and 2,600 direct to the co-packer Rivermark Kits in Fresno. Use-by dates run to October 19, and about 40 percent has already sold through. The weak points are the MES-to-WMS interface and Rivermark's partly paper records.
overview.operationalImpact: At 06:00 the Recall Team call opens on the bridge, and the hold and trace targets have been running since 05:50. Plant 1 stops line 2 for sanitation and a swab series. DC crews in Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas have to find, count and segregate held pallets. Dallas has already shipped 2,100 cases to 38 Cornerstone Grocers stores since 04:00. A Sonoran Cold Freight trailer near Tucson carries 1,320 cases and is 14 hours from Dallas, so dispatchers have to decide whether to reroute or hold it. The counts don't agree: MES shows 38,600 cases, a WMS export shows 38,540 and a draft press release says "about 40,000". Rivermark cannot quickly match its paper receiving records to the lots (the last mock recall left 4 percent unmatched), and its Caesar kits have gone on to national retail accounts. At 09:30 CDPH calls about three reported illnesses with a genetic match pending and asks for the distribution list. An FDA records request starts a 24-hour clock for the sortable spreadsheet. At 11:00 a food safety blogger posts that "romaine is about to be recalled." The President must decide the recall class, depth and public warning before confirmation arrives. Customer service reps must reach Harvest Table Markets (212 stores), Cornerstone Grocers (140 Texas stores) and Westline Foodservice (31 delivery points, including hospitals and school districts) within 4 hours of that decision. Cornerstone threatens to drop Pinecrest and demands replacement romaine, but supply chain can cover only about 60 percent of romaine volume within 48 hours. A Central Coast Courier reporter calls before the press release, which needs the retailers' agreement, can go out.

overview.targetAudience: Food safety and quality (Recall Coordinator), supply chain planning and allocation, logistics and distribution, traceability and enterprise systems (MES/ERP/WMS), customer service, and corporate communications
overview.location: Pinecrest Fresh Cut, LLC — Plant 1 conference room and Recall Team bridge

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to build and present a recall recommendation to the President (proposed class, depth, the five PF1 lot codes, quantity and whether a public warning is needed) on a presumptive E. coli O157:H7 result, before lab confirmation, as PPHTRP 4 requires.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to bring the MES (38,600 cases), the WMS export (38,540) and Rivermark Kits' paper receiving records into one reconciliation table, as PLCTR 8 requires, within the 4-hour internal trace target, and to deliver the FDA sortable spreadsheet within its 24-hour clock.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep the PFC-FS-04 2 notification order (plant and DCs, then FDA and CDPH, then customers, then the press release) while CDPH asks for the distribution list, a blogger posts early and a Central Coast Courier reporter calls before the release has retailer agreement.

objectives.name: Operational Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to confirm physical holds at the Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas DCs within 4 hours, decide what to do with the Sonoran Cold Freight trailer near Tucson and the 2,100 cases already sent to Cornerstone stores, and allocate the roughly 60 percent replacement romaine supply among customers.

roles.name: VP Food Safety and Quality (Recall Coordinator)
roles.team: Team A: Food Safety and Quality
roles.description: Owns the hold, the recall recommendation to the President, contact with FDA and CDPH, the contact log and the reconciled case counts for the incident.
standingOrders: Hold Now: place lot holds in the MES within 30 minutes of a signal, without waiting for confirmation or approval.
Protect Health: if a product may cause serious illness, propose Class I at consumer level with a public warning, even while the lab result is still presumptive.
One Number: no count goes to FDA, a customer or the press until the reconciliation table matches the MES.
Log Everything: record who spoke to each regulator, what was said and when.

roles.name: VP Supply Chain
roles.description: Manages stopping shipments of lots that may share the cause and filling unaffected demand from other lots, including allocating limited replacement romaine among customers.
standingOrders: Containment First: stop every shipment that may share the cause before filling any order, whatever the customer pressure.
Allocate Openly: split the roughly 60 percent replacement supply by a stated rule, not by whichever customer shouts loudest.
Clean Lots Only: fill replacement orders only from lots the Traceability and Systems Lead has cleared.

roles.name: Director of Logistics
roles.description: Manages DC holds and segregation, trailers in transit, and the return or destruction of held product with certificates.
standingOrders: Trust the Floor: a hold counts only when pallets are physically found, tagged and counted at the DC, whatever the WMS shows.
Keep It Cold: hold segregated product at 34 to 38 degrees Fahrenheit until disposition, never dump it early.
Stop the Truck: when a trailer carries suspect lots, hold or reroute it to quarantine rather than let it deliver to stores.

roles.name: Traceability and Systems Lead
roles.description: Owns the lot trace across MES, WMS and co-packer records, the reconciliation table and the FDA sortable spreadsheet.
standingOrders: Verify Before Release: mark every unreconciled case as unaccounted for instead of smoothing over the gap.
Beat the Clock: the 4-hour internal trace target comes first; the FDA 24-hour deadline is the outer limit.
Keep One Format: every record uses the PF<plant>-<yy><ddd>-L<line>-<shift> lot code format, with nothing approximated.

roles.name: Customer Service Manager
roles.description: Manages customer phone calls, recall letters, acknowledgment tracking and effectiveness checks across Harvest Table, Cornerstone, Westline and Rivermark.
standingOrders: Four Hours: reach every direct customer's food safety contact by phone and email within 4 hours of the recall decision.
Chase Silence: call back every customer that has not acknowledged within 24 hours.
No Side Deals: never promise replacement volume or credits that Supply Chain has not confirmed.

roles.name: Communications Manager
roles.description: Manages the press release, the consumer notice on the website, holding statements and media enquiries.
standingOrders: Order Matters: the press release posts only after customers are told, unless a public health agency announces first; then it goes within one hour.
Facts From the Coordinator: publish no count or lot code the Recall Coordinator has not confirmed from the reconciliation table.
Truth Over Reassurance: a holding statement says what is not yet known instead of minimizing the risk.

phases.title: The Presumptive
phases.goal: Tests whether the Recall Team treats an unconfirmed lab result as a recall signal under PPHTRP 3, sets the scope by the PPHTRP 5 rules, and gets hold notices to Plant 1 and the three DCs within the 30-minute target in PFC-FS-04 2.
beats: (06:00) The Recall Team bridge opens. The SimCell replays the 05:50 Coastal Analytical Labs email: presumptive E. coli O157:H7 on a retained sample of PF1-27278-L2-B, with confirmation 24 to 48 hours out. The Recall Coordinator must record 05:50 as the signal time and recognize that the 06:20 hold-notice deadline is already close.

(06:10) The Recall Coordinator applies the PPHTRP 5 scope rules: every lot made on line 2 within 24 hours of the positive, plus raw material lot FLD-SLG-R14-C-27277 from Santa Lucia Growers Ranch 14 Block C. That gives five lots: PF1-27277-L2-B, PF1-27278-L2-A, PF1-27278-L2-B, PF1-27279-L2-A and PF1-27279-L2-B. The Plant 1 manager (SimCell) reports that line 2 has stopped for sanitation and a swab series.
(06:15) Noise item: the Stockton DC reports a reefer alarm on dock door 7 that has nothing to do with the recall. Players must decide whether it needs attention or is a distraction.

(06:35) First technical note: the MES hold on the five lots was placed at 06:12, but the Dallas DC WMS still shows those lots as pickable. Under PLCTR 4 the MES-to-WMS interface should block picking within 10 minutes, and it has not. The Dallas DC manager adds that 2,100 cases went out to 38 Cornerstone Grocers stores after 04:00, before the hold existed.

phases.title: Counts Don't Agree
phases.goal: Tests the Traceability and Systems Lead and Director of Logistics on building one reconciliation table from the MES, WMS and Rivermark paper records under PLCTR 5. It also tests whether the team can confirm physical holds at Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas while outside parties push for data.
beats: (Time jump to 09:00) The data problem has spread. MES shows 38,600 cases and the WMS export shows 38,540, a 60-case gap. A draft press release in circulation says "about 40,000". The split is 18,900 cases at Stockton, 9,700 at Phoenix, 7,400 at Dallas and 2,600 at Rivermark Kits. The Traceability and Systems Lead must list the gaps in the separate tab with a reason for each (scan failure, manual re-label, paper record), as PLCTR 5 requires.

Red herring: a WMS administrator (SimCell) suggests the 60-case gap and the interface lag are a cyberattack on the ERP–WMS interface and wants it taken offline. Some players want to escalate to IT security. Others see the ordinary roughly 1 percent scan-failure rate from PLCTR 4 and a 15-minute interface delay.
Visual for the room: a DC hold-status board. Stockton and Phoenix show pallets physically segregated and counted. Dallas shows 'held in system / not physically confirmed' for its remaining pallets.

Rivermark Kits (SimCell) faxes partly handwritten receiving logs. It cannot match the 2,600 cases to lot codes quickly (its last mock recall left 4 percent unmatched), and its Caesar kits have already gone to national retail accounts. The Rivermark Kits vendor estimates a full match by end of day, which nobody on the team believes.

(09:30) CDPH Food and Drug Branch calls: three reported illnesses, genetic match pending, and a request for the distribution list now. Separately, an FDA records request starts the 24-hour clock for the PLCTR 5 sortable spreadsheet. The Recall Coordinator must review any sheet before it goes out.

phases.title: Recall Before Confirmation
phases.goal: Tests the one decision point. The Recall Coordinator must present the President with a recommended class, recall depth, the five PF1 lot codes, the reconciled quantity and whether to issue a public warning, before lab confirmation (PPHTRP 4). The phase then tests whether the team holds the PFC-FS-04 2 notification order while outside pressure builds.
beats: (11:00) A food safety blogger posts that "romaine is about to be recalled". Social chatter climbs, and Harvest Table Markets calls Customer Service asking whether the post is true.

DECISION POINT (11:15): the President (SimCell) asks for the recommendation. Option one: recall now at consumer level with a public warning and a proposed Class I, and risk a wasted recall and lost customers if confirmation comes back negative. Option two: hold quietly and wait 24 to 48 hours, accepting illness risk at retail while about 40 percent of the product has sold through and use-by dates run to October 19. Whichever way they decide, the quantity must come from the reconciliation table, not the press-release draft.

Logistics workarounds: the Director of Logistics must decide whether to reroute or hold in place the Sonoran Cold Freight trailer near Tucson, which carries 1,320 cases and is 14 hours from Dallas. Players must also arrange manual store-level pulls of the 2,100 cases at 38 Cornerstone Grocers stores and staff the Dallas physical hold count.

Partner friction: Cornerstone Grocers threatens to drop Pinecrest and demands replacement romaine, but Supply chain can cover only about 60 percent of volume within 48 hours. The VP Supply Chain must allocate it among Harvest Table Markets, Cornerstone and Westline Foodservice, whose 31 delivery points include hospitals and school districts, under PFC-FS-04 7.

(11:40) A Central Coast Courier reporter calls with a 13:00 deadline. The press release does not yet have retailer agreement, so the Communications Manager must hold the order in PFC-FS-04 2. The order changes if CDPH announces first, because then customers and the press release must go within one hour.

phases.title: Notify and Verify
phases.goal: Tests whether the team carries out the notifications in order with one consistent set of numbers, verifies that holds and the reconciliation are real before relying on them, and handles the legal and regulatory follow-up before ENDEX.
beats: Notifications go out in order. Customer Service calls the food safety and category contacts at Harvest Table Markets, Cornerstone Grocers and Westline Foodservice, using the PFC-FS-04 7 script. Recall letters go by email and courier within 4 hours of the decision. Westline and Rivermark Kits are told to notify their own downstream customers and send their lists within 12 hours.

Hurdle: IT restarts the MES-to-WMS interface to clear the lag, and the restart re-sends an old file. The Dallas WMS briefly shows PF1-27279-L2-A as released and pickable. A Dallas picker scans a held pallet before a supervisor stops it.

Verification: before any count goes into a letter, release or the FDA spreadsheet, the Recall Coordinator must check three things. Physical hold confirmations from Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas must match the system. The sheet totals must equal the 38,600 cases produced in the MES, as PLCTR 5 requires. Rivermark Kits' unmatched cases must be listed in the gaps tab and must not be left out.

Legal and regulatory follow-up: the General Counsel (SimCell) confirms notice to Trellis Mutual and checks Supply contracts for notice duties under PPHTRP 8. The Recall Coordinator confirms whether a Reportable Food Registry entry is due within 24 hours and sets the date for the first FDA status report.

(10:00 elapsed, approx. 13:45 narrative time) Customer acknowledgment tracker: Westline has not responded about two school-district delivery points, so the team schedules call-backs. The Recall Coordinator records hot-wash notes on the interface fault and on Rivermark Kits' paper records. ENDEX.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The Recall Coordinator has to build the recall recommendation from a presumptive result before confirmation, take it to the President and get a logged decision. That is the decision chain PPHTRP 4.3 sets out.
The recommendation has to state whether a public warning is needed. PPHTRP 4.3 says a product that may cause serious illness is proposed as Class I, at consumer level, with a public warning.

The objective tests whether MES, WMS and Rivermark Kits' paper records can be traced and reconciled to every consignee within 4 hours. The trace must produce the PLCTR 5 sortable spreadsheet with a gaps tab and deliver it to FDA within 24 hours.

Pinecrest has to keep the PFC-FS-04 2 order (holds first, then FDA and CDPH, then customers, then the press release) while a blogger posts early, a reporter calls and retailers demand to approve the release.

The Recall Coordinator has to coordinate contacts with FDA and CDPH, the CDPH request for the distribution list, and the timing of any CDPH announcement. These contacts set when customer notices and the release can go out.

The team has to confirm physical holds at the DCs, stop or redirect the Sonoran Cold Freight trailer and stop shipments of the five lots. It must also fill unaffected demand and allocate the limited replacement romaine among customers.
The objective requires coordinated holds across Plant 1 and the Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas DCs under the Recall Coordinator's MES hold and hold notices.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room one team at a time (Recall Team, QA/traceability, logistics/DCs, customer service, communications) and write each answer on the whiteboard in two columns so the room can see patterns before the discussion questions start.

questions.text: At I-13 the President said, "Somebody tell me which number is real," after seeing 38,600 cases in the MES, 38,540 in the WMS export, and "about 40,000" in conversation. When did you stop trusting the MES-to-WMS interface? Who explained the 60-case gap to the decision-makers, and in what words? Did operations understand what the technical team was saying, and did the technical team understand what operations needed in order to act? What would have let you put one reconciled number in front of the President within the 4-hour trace target?

At I-05 and again in the I-10 fax, Delia at Rivermark Kits gave you handwritten clipboard entries like 'PF1-278-L2' with no shift letter, a crossed-out '27277?', and 104 unmatched cases. She also told you 3,850 Caesar kits had already shipped to national retail accounts. Did you treat those clipboard photocopies as evidence that needed to go into your reconciliation table, or as a ticket to close once the office manager sent a clean match? When she asked whether to hold everything with romaine or only the lots she could match, and whether you wanted her downstream customer list now or later, what did you answer and why? When did Rivermark become a partner on your trace instead of just a recipient of your hold notice?

At I-13, with a presumptive positive, three CDPH illnesses, and no confirmation for at least 24 hours, the President asked for your recommendation: class, depth, the five PF1 lot codes, quantity, and whether to issue a public warning. What did you actually recommend, and how confident were you in the lot codes and case count you gave? What were you waiting for that you didn't really need? Looking back, what information or pre-agreed decision rule would have let you make that call faster and with less argument?

By I-19, a post showing a spinach bag labeled PF1-27284-L3-A had 1,100 shares. Channel 8 wanted confirmation before its noon show, CDPH wanted the distribution list, and Harvest Table would not agree to a press release unless it saw the text by 10:30 and the release said spinach was not included. What did you say publicly, or to reporters, before your facts were confirmed? Did you keep the order in PFC-FS-04 Section 2 (plant and DCs, then FDA and CDPH, then customers, then the press release), or did outside pressure decide who heard first? Did the lot codes and counts stay the same across every message you sent?

At I-14, Cornerstone demanded 100 percent replacement volume by Thursday and written confirmation by 10:00. You also had the Westline standing order for 6 hospitals and 4 school districts, only about 60 percent of normal volume available, and open questions about the Sonoran Cold Freight trailer near Tucson and the 2,100 cases already at Cornerstone stores. How did you decide who got the replacement romaine? Did the loudest customer set your priorities, or did public health? When did you get physical confirmation that product was on hold at the Stockton, Phoenix and Dallas DCs, as opposed to an email saying the hold was in place?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. The aim is to test the Recall Team's plans and procedures, not to judge individual players.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players should not challenge the lab result, the illness reports or the system data. They should work with what the injects show.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures (PPHTRP, PLCTR and PFC-FS-04). Where a plan is silent or unclear, players should say what they would do and note the gap for the hot wash.
Players know only what the module narrative and the injects tell them. Information arrives as it would on the bridge, by phone, email, radio and screen.
Players fill their own seats on the Recall Team. Decisions that belong to the President or the General Counsel are made by those roles as played by the SimCell.
artificialities: Time is compressed: the four one-hour modules cover 06:00 to 10:00 Pacific Time on October 12, 2027, and time-jump cards move the clock forward between modules.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes Coastal Analytical Labs, CDPH, FDA, the Plant 1 Manager, the DC managers and staff, the WMS administrator, Rivermark Kits, Harvest Table, Cornerstone, Westline, Sonoran Cold Freight, the President, the General Counsel, Trellis Mutual, reporters and members of the public.

The MES, ERP, the three DC WMS systems, the MES-to-WMS interface and the PFC-OPS-02 screens are named as they appear in the plans, but nobody touches them. Holds, exports and interface actions are simulated and reported through injects.

Injects arrive on paper or on screen as emails, faxes, screenshots, status boards, social media posts and phone slips. Calls are role-played on the simulated bridge. No real notice goes to FDA, CDPH, customers, insurers or the media.
Lab confirmation, swab results and the WGS findings stay outstanding for the whole exercise. Players must make their decisions without them.

**Module 2: Counts Don't Agree (07:00–08:00 PT)**

It is 07:00 Pacific Time. The fog has not lifted. Line 2 was stopped at 06:04 and is still down while a swab series runs. A presumptive positive for E. coli O157:H7 on retained lot PF1-27278-L2-B came in at 05:50, and confirmation is 24 to 48 hours away. The MES has shown holds on five lots since 06:12: PF1-27277-L2-B, PF1-27278-L2-A, PF1-27278-L2-B, PF1-27279-L2-A and PF1-27279-L2-B, plus raw lot FLD-SLG-R14-C-27277.

The Dallas WMS showed two of those lots as pickable at 06:34, and three MES-to-WMS messages were stuck in the queue. Dallas had shipped 2,100 cases to 38 Cornerstone stores since 04:00. A Sonoran Cold Freight trailer with 1,320 more cases is near Tucson. Rivermark Kits received 2,600 cases but logs lots on paper, some without a shift letter, and some Caesar kits have already gone out. A worker's post about Line 2 is circulating, and Cornerstone wants answers.

The MES shows 38,600 cases: Stockton 18,900, Phoenix 9,700, Dallas 7,400 and Rivermark 2,600. The 06:52 WMS export shows 38,540, so 60 cases are missing. A draft press release saying "about 40,000 cases", saved by an unknown editor, has been forwarded twice. The DCs have until 09:50 to confirm physical holds.

Is the interface fault a security problem, and is shutting the interface down worth the loss of hold messages?
Dallas cannot physically confirm its held stock before the 4-hour window closes.
CDPH and FDA both want data now, before the counts are clean.
An uncontrolled draft press release with an unverified number is spreading.

**Module 3: Recall Before Confirmation (08:00–09:00 PT)**

It is 08:00 Pacific Time, and the fog is starting to thin. CDPH has reported three E. coli O157:H7 illnesses, two in Sacramento County and one in Reno; whole-genome sequencing is pending. FDA's records request for the five PF1 lots and lot FLD-SLG-R14-C-27277 has been in the inbox since 07:34.
